newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil dragged higher by IPE futures.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil dragged higher by IPE futures.

text.p: NWE gas oil rose on Monday but the price range was more a reflection of benchmark IPE gas oil gains rather than any pick-up in the physical market, traders said.
July gas oil settled $1.75 higher at $160.25 a tonne, having shed $4.0 over the course of last week.
The physical market, however, was subdued.
"The futures gains have helped demand a bit," said one trader. "But we have to wait and see whether these gains are sustained."
A couple of parcels of heating oil traded at July IPE -25 cents fob ARA for June delivery. Traders pegged premiums at around July IPE -50 cents/flat.
Low sulphur barges traded at July IPE +$5.25 fob ARA and there was talk that material was done out of Antwerp at July IPE +$4.75.
Russian cargo premiums remained in negative territory at around July IPE -$1.00/-50 cents cif NWE, a slight improvement on last week when diffs were quoted around -$1.50/+$1.00.
EN590 material stagnated at last weeks levels of July IPE +$5.00/+$5.50 cif NWE.
